title: Proposal for a Council Recommendation on common principles on regulatory sandboxes to support innovation and a future-proof regulatory framework (COM(2026) 568)
date_evidence: Commission proposal dated 9.9.2026; Council cover page dated 10 September 2026
key_claim: The Commission found 132 regulatory sandboxes at national level across 15 Member States, up from 40 in the 2021 survey, and proposes a non-binding Council Recommendation under which derogations from applicable Union secondary law are envisaged only where Union acts already provide for them.
frame_summary: The Commission promotes sandboxes as a growing tool but proposes a non-binding principle set that does not itself create any power to waive Union rules.
verbatim_quote: This second survey identified 132 regulatory sandboxes at national level, across 15 Member States
verbatim_list: ensure that derogations from applicable Union secondary law are envisaged only where the possibility for such derogations is provided for in applicable Union acts
given the non-binding legal nature of the proposed instrument
notes: Council document ST 12971/26, English text, fetched via WebFetch 12/10/2026. Quote segments were returned split by the extractor's length limit; joined here without added words.

publisher: GOV.UK (Advisory AI Growth Lab, legal services)
title: Legal services advisory AI Growth Lab: overview
key_claim: The UK's advisory AI Growth Lab gives innovators coordinated access to regulators; participation does not provide regulatory approval, endorsement or exemptions from legal obligations; applications close 27 September 2026.
frame_summary: The UK government describes its AI Growth Lab as a route to regulator explanation of existing rules, expressly not a route to exemption.
verbatim_quote: Participation does not provide regulatory approval, endorsement or exemptions from legal obligations.
verbatim_list: Applications are now open and will close at 11:59pm on 27 September 2026.
notes: Page first published 03/08/2026, last public update 27/08/2026.

title: Independent review of the Enhanced Regulatory Sandbox: Government response
date_evidence: Publication date 07 September 2026 on https://treasury.gov.au/publication/p2026-802423; the PDF date line reads September 2026
key_claim: The Government agrees to progress repeal of the current ERS legislation and regulations so ASIC can design a more flexible replacement using its existing relief powers.
frame_summary: The Australian Government accepts the review's view that the statutory sandbox should go and be replaced by an ASIC-designed regime built on its discretionary relief powers.
verbatim_quote: Progress repeal of the current ERS legislation and regulations
verbatim_list: The Government agrees to all recommendations directed to it

title: Exploring State AI Governance in AGORA #2: AI Regulatory Sandboxes
key_claim: US states including Delaware, Utah and Texas have adopted AI regulatory sandboxes; Texas lets participants test for three years without authorisation and shields them from enforcement for waived laws, and Utah agreements include waived regulations.
frame_summary: A tracker of US state AI law shows a small group of states writing sandboxes that can waive regulation, in contrast to advisory models.
verbatim_quote: States including Delaware, Utah, and Texas have adopted AI regulatory sandboxes.
verbatim_list: without obtaining a regulatory authorization for three years
for violation of laws or regulations waived by the sandbox policies
geographic reach, technical safeguards, and waived regulations
notes: Counter-evidence source: waiver-capable statutory sandboxes exist in some US states.

title: Enhanced Regulatory Sandbox review
key_claim: Since 2020 ASIC received 103 applications to the ERS and accepted 19 entities (18% of applicants); only one former participant has obtained an AFSL after exiting.
frame_summary: An Australian law firm summarises the review's finding that the statutory sandbox admitted few firms and offered little route to a licence.
verbatim_quote: Only one former participant has obtained an AFSL after exiting the sandbox.
verbatim_list: accepted 19 entities (18% of applicants) into the ERS
notes: Law-firm commentary on the independent review; page metadata carries earlier dates but the visible date line is 15 September 2026.

title: Government backs Enhanced Regulatory Sandbox overhaul
key_claim: The Government will repeal the legislation underpinning the ERS and let ASIC build a replacement using existing relief powers; FinTech Australia calls the move a positive step.
frame_summary: Specialist financial press reports the repeal as a policy overhaul that industry welcomes for its promise of thematic sandboxes.
verbatim_quote: agreeing to repeal the legislation underpinning the Enhanced Regulatory Sandbox (ERS)
verbatim_list: This is a positive step and enabling more innovation through thematic sandboxes will help fintechs
notes: Counter-evidence: industry reads the change as positive.

title: DSIT opens AI Growth Lab sandbox to legal services
key_claim: Regulators attached to the UK AI Growth Lab explain how existing rules apply rather than write new ones; the open test is whether advice given inside the lab carries weight outside it.
frame_summary: A trade news item stresses that the UK lab is advisory and questions whether its advice will bind regulators once a product launches.
verbatim_quote: The test for this one is whether regulator advice given inside the lab carries weight outside it
verbatim_list: Their role is to explain how existing rules apply to AI tools rather than to write new ones
